body:
I am not strictly against this, but I feel some doubt about it.

I've previously [suggested](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/5299#issuecomment-1233150372) a more generic shorthand for `[code]something[/code]`, but now I'm even more hesitant about that than I am about your approach. BBCode is a very simple but verbose markup, unlike Markdown, wiki markup, and RestructuredText. So shorthand like `[[something]]` feels alien, like an incomplete step toward Markdown-like markup.

The `[null]`, `[false]`, and `[true]` shorthands seem more organic to the markup we have, but I have some doubts. None of them are critical, but still.

1. BBCode is not meant to be short, opening and closing tags take up a lot of space (see XML vs JSON). If we are trying to introduce such shortcuts, doesn't that mean BBCode is not well suited for the task? Maybe we should consider replacing BBCode with some other format in the future (say in 5.0)?
2. Currently, `[tag]` can be either a syntactic construct or a class name. For example, we don't have a `[class Node]` tag, instead we just write `[Node]`. This PR extends the use of the bracket construct to special values ​​(in addition to types), potentially opening up the possibility for other shortcuts. For example, `[0]`, `[-1]`, `[0.0]`, `[""]`, `["name"]`, etc.
3. This somewhat harms cross-version compatibility of engine and extension/addon documentation. Yes, this can be overcome over time, but at first it will still be preferable to use the old option.

Just to note that I understand that this would be useful because it is used so often. Perhaps we should still make an exception here, despite conceptual and compatibility concerns. But appearance and clickability are worth discussing.

> This is a draft because it's not implemented for the online docs and I really don't know how, at the moment.

You need to make similar changes to `make_rst.py` and `modules/mono/editor/bindings_generator.cpp`:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a0cd8f187a43935d756e49bf3778f39f0964f0ac/doc/tools/make_rst.py#L1859

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a0cd8f187a43935d756e49bf3778f39f0964f0ac/modules/mono/editor/bindings_generator.cpp#L175

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a0cd8f187a43935d756e49bf3778f39f0964f0ac/modules/mono/editor/bindings_generator.cpp#L437

> BBCode is a very simple but verbose markup, unlike Markdown, wiki markup, and RestructuredText. So shorthand like [[something]] feels alien, like an incomplete step toward Markdown-like markup.

Hard agree, but at the same time, as you mention later:

> Currently, `[tag]` can be either a syntactic construct or a class name. For example, we don't have a `[class Node]` tag, instead we just write `[Node]`.

There's a precedent to this in the class reference format, and it's also pretty much Godot-exclusive.

> This somewhat harms cross-version compatibility of engine and extension/addon documentation. Yes, this can be overcome over time, but at first it will still be preferable to use the old option.

With this point, any change to the class reference's BBCode format _right now_ is not possible. I do agree it's ideal to achieve this, however.

> BBCode is not meant to be short, opening and closing tags take up a lot of space (see XML vs JSON). If we are trying to introduce such shortcuts, doesn't that mean BBCode is not well suited for the task? Maybe we should consider replacing BBCode with some other format in the future (say in 5.0)?

Unironically, yes. Replacing BBCode with something Markdown-like would be awesome in a far, breaking future and I think it would benefit everyone. Contributors (that use GitHub's syntax out of habit), translators (WebLate itself supports it, or similar), and developers (Markdown is easier to write and read, even when not unformatted). There's no proposal on this but I had it in mind for a really long time.
The built-in editor help already has to go through a huge conversion step before displaying the text. As you are aware, it does not just parse the written BBCode into the **RichTextLabel**.

> Replacing BBCode with something Markdown-like would be awesome in a far, breaking future and I think it would benefit everyone.

Markdown cannot do everything BBCode do - even if you use HTML within Markdown, you can only choose between "high-level Markdown" and "low-level HTML" (and you can't use Markdown within HTML tags). There is no middle ground like with BBCode where you can have your own tags that accept parameters. Some static site generators like Hugo support their own [shortcode](https://gohugo.io/content-management/shortcodes/) syntax to extend Markdown, but there is no accepted standard here.

If Markdown to be implemented, it would likely be done through Markdown-to-BBCode conversion and could be supported in documentation comments (as it's more readable in raw form than BBCode). But for the class reference XML itself, I would stick to BBCode to avoid breaking translations.
